entry.title: Antithesis Develops System Capable of Beating NetHack
entry.content:
Links: antithesis.com | lobsters | hacker news

Antithesis has developed a system capable of finding a path to victory in NetHack within five minutes on approximately 80% of game seeds. The approach utilizes a computing paradigm similar to probabilistic programming to allow agents to navigate the game's extensive state space and long-horizon planning requirements.

The development process integrated technical lessons learned from training agents on other titles, such as Super Mario Bros., Zelda, and Tetris. These experiences helped the team refine core mechanisms including value functions, resource management, and the pruning of doomed game states.

entry.title: European Commission Proposes Digital Fairness Act with New Restrictions on Video Games
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | ec.europa.eu

The European Commission has released its proposal for the Digital Fairness Act, introducing strict consumer protection rules that target monetization and user experience design in video games across European Union member states. The 71-page legislative proposal includes sweeping restrictions on free-to-play features, requiring transparent real-money values for virtual currencies, prohibiting certain pay-to-win mechanisms for minors, and banning the sale of loot boxes to underage players entirely.

Additional provisions require companies to allow users to disable compulsive design elements such as push notifications and engagement streaks, while virtual currencies and in-app purchases targeting minors will be disabled by default. European industry trade bodies, including Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation, have criticized the proposal, arguing that its broad definitions and age-rating criteria could heavily disrupt game development and balancing before the bill faces a formal vote in the European Parliament and Council.

entry.title: CD Projekt Red Uses AI Voice Tools to Help Jacek Rozenek Reprise Geralt in The Witcher 3 Expansion
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | gamefile.news

CD Projekt Red is utilizing AI voice technology from Respeecher to help actor Jacek Rozenek reprise his role as Geralt of Rivia in the upcoming Witcher 3: Wild Hunt expansion, Songs of the Past. Rozenek suffered a stroke that altered his voice, and the studio received his consent to use AI to bridge the gap between his current performances and thousands of lines recorded over a decade ago for the 2015 game.

Localization producer Mikołaj Szwed emphasized that the decision was an ethical exception made strictly due to Rozenek's health constraints. CD Projekt Red previously used Respeecher to recreate the voice of a late actor for the Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty, but this marks a distinct application aimed at maintaining performance continuity for a living actor.

entry.content:

Layoffs were most prevalent in AAA studios, affecting 68% of companies, and primarily impacted roles in quality assurance, marketing/PR, and visual or technical arts. While many displaced workers found new employment, only 68% remained in a similar field, and 9% reported leaving the game industry entirely.

He argued that the console's architecture is frustrating because it is similar to the Xbox Series X but has significantly lower memory and performance, forcing developers to perform extra optimization work to ensure compatibility across both versions.
